en: The Apadāna of the Elder Saṅghupaṭṭhāka Kumuda Chapter 10.10 I was a monk in the dispensation of the Buddha Padumuttara; I was a preacher of the Dhamma, possessed of great wisdom. To that elder who was preaching the Dhamma, I approached him and sat down at one side. Having heard his excellent discourse on the Dhamma, I made this aspiration for the sake of my own welfare: "May I, in a future time, become a preacher of the Dhamma and may I be as wise as this elder. Having made this aspiration, I passed away from there; after passing through various births, I was reborn in heaven. From there, having passed away, I was reborn in the human world; having performed wholesome deeds, I attained the state of a deva. For eighty-four thousand aeons I dwelt in the realm of the Thirty-three. From there, having passed away, I was reborn in the human world; I was a king named Mahāpabbata, a lord of the earth. In that same dispensation, I was a monk; I was a preacher of the Dhamma, possessed of great wisdom. I preached the Dhamma to the multitude of people; I was honored by the Sangha, like a leader of the assembly. Having lived the holy life under the dispensation of Kassapa, I passed away from here and was reborn in the Brahma-world. After passing through various births, I was reborn in the human world; I am now the Elder Saṅghupaṭṭhāka, a preacher of the Dhamma. By this root of merit, may I never fall into the lower realms; may I always be a preacher of the Dhamma, possessed of great wisdom. May I preach the Dhamma to the multitude of people; may I be honored by the Sangha, like a leader of the assembly. Through this wholesome deed, may I never fall into the lower realms; may I always be a preacher of the Dhamma, possessed of great wisdom. May I preach the Dhamma to the multitude of people; may I be honored by the Sangha, like a leader of the assembly. Thus did I speak these words, and the Exalted One replied: "You shall preach the Dhamma to the multitude of people; you shall be honored by the Sangha, like a leader of the assembly. “During the time of the Blessed One Vessabhū,
I was a monastery attendant;
with a clear mind and joyful heart, I served him.”
I attended upon the supreme Saṅgha.
Thirty-one eons ago,
that deed which I performed then—
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of my attendance.
In the seventh aeon from now,
There were seven [kings] who ruled over the earth to its ocean limits;
they were wheel-turning monarchs of great power, endowed with the seven treasures.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Saṅghupaṭṭhāka speak these verses.
This is the tenth legend of the elder Saṅghupaṭṭhāka.
The eighteenth chapter, the Kumuda Chapter, is concluded.
Its summary verse:
Kumuda, then Nisseṇī,
Rattika, and Udapānado.
The lion-throned giver of the path,
the solitary lamp, the one whose foot is a jewel;
the physician, the attendant.
"Five and ten verses."
